description: Given two sparse matrices mat1 (m x k) and mat2 (k x n), return their product. A sparse matrix has mostly zero elements.
intuition: For sparse matrices, most multiplications involve zero and are wasted work. The key optimization is simple: skip zeros. If mat1[i][j] is zero, skip the entire inner loop. This turns a dense O(mkn) operation into something much faster for sparse data.
approach: Skip zero elements during multiplication. For each non-zero element mat1[i][j], multiply it with each non-zero mat2[j][k] and accumulate into the result.
explanation:
1. Initialize result matrix of size m x n with zeros.
2. For each element mat1[i][j], skip if zero.
3. For each element mat2[j][l], skip if zero.
4. Accumulate mat1[i][j] * mat2[j][l] into result[i][l].
5. Skipping zeros makes this efficient for sparse matrices.
timeComplexity: O(m * k * n) worst case, much better for sparse matrices
hints: The key optimization for sparse matrices is skipping zero elements.
If mat1[i][j] is 0, skip the entire inner loop for that element.
Pre-process sparse representation if needed for very sparse matrices.
